verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents client-credentials service accounts that let applications and services, and so an agent, obtain access on their own behalf rather than a user's. It also documents role-based and fine-grained resource-level authorization policies for restricting what those credentials can reach, and a revocation endpoint for killing tokens. missing for 10: explicit docs on per-client OAuth scope restriction applied to a service-account credential, agent-specific delegation guidance (e.g., token exchange), and independent or hands-on corroboration of least-privilege agent setups.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Client Credentials are used when clients (applications and services) want to obtain access on behalf of themselves rather than on behalf of a user.

Keycloak provides fine-grained authorization services as well. This allows you to manage permissions for all your services from the Keycloak admin console and gives you the power to define exactly the policies you need.
The token revocation endpoint is used to revoke tokens. Both refresh tokens and access tokens are supported by this endpoint.
